 2027 Medicare Part B Premium Increase Smaller Than Social Security COLA
 Standard Part B premiums will rise 3.2% to $209.40 per month, marking the first time since 2023 that the increase trails Social Security's annual cost of living adjustment
 By Brian Anderson 
 | 
 November 18, 2026 
 | 
 2 minute read 
 Share

 X

 Email 
 Copy URL 
 Prefer us on Google 
 Image credit: © Maria Dryfhout | Dreamstime.com 
 Medicare Part B Premiums will rise by 3.2% in 2027, increasing by $6.50 per month to $209.40, the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS)  announced  on Nov. 17.
 “The increase in the 2027 Part B standard premium and deductible is mainly due to projected increases in healthcare spending.”
 Nov. 17 CMS announcement 
 That increase from $202.90 in 2026 to $209.40 equates to a $78 annual increase, and means seniors will pay $2,512.80 total for the year.
 Notably, 2027 marks the first time since 2023 that the percentage increase in the standard Medicare Part B premium (3.2%) is smaller than the annual Social Security cost of living adjustment (COLA), which the Social Security Administration announced Oct. 14 would be  3.6% for 2027 . In 2023, the standard Part B premium actually fell 3.1%, while Social Security beneficiaries received an 8.7% COLA.
 Shannon Benton, executive director of The Senior Citizens League, said that although the 2027 COLA is higher than the Part B premium increase, seniors should not assume that means they are getting ahead financially.
 “The average retired worker’s Social Security benefit is expected to increase by approximately $75 per month, but the additional $6.50 in Part B premiums will immediately reduce that increase for beneficiaries whose premiums are deducted from their checks,” Benton told  401(k) Specialist .
 “And Part B is only one piece of the puzzle. Seniors are also facing rising costs for prescription drugs, supplemental insurance, housing, utilities, groceries, and other necessities. The list goes on and on,” Benton added. “Social Security’s COLA is intended to help retirees maintain their purchasing power, not simply help them keep up with rising Medicare costs. TSCL believes seniors deserve a more meaningful measure of inflation that reflects the expenses they actually face in retirement. Retirees should not have to sacrifice other basic necessities just to afford their health coverage.”
 Each year, the Medicare Part B premium, deductible, and coinsurance rates are determined according to provisions of the Social Security Act. Medicare Part B covers physicians’ services, outpatient hospital services, certain home health services, durable medical equipment, and certain other medical and health services not covered by Medicare Part A.
 The annual deductible for all Medicare Part B beneficiaries will be $292 in 2027, an increase of $9 from the annual deductible of $283 in 2026.
 “The increase in the 2027 Part B standard premium and deductible is mainly due to projected increases in healthcare spending,” Tuesday’s CMS announcement stated.
 The 3.2% 2027 increase in the Part B premium is a significant decline from the premium increase of  9.7% in 2026 , and also the 5.9% increase in 2025.
 IRMAA cutoffs 
 The CMS announcement noted that since 2007, a beneficiary’s Part B monthly premium has been based on income. For 2027, that means individuals with modified adjusted gross income higher than $112,000 (and couples with MAGI over $224,000) will face even higher monthly costs, impacting roughly 9% of people with Medicare Part B. 
 The 2027 income-related monthly adjustment amount, or IRMAA, are 2.75% higher than the 2026 cutoffs of $109,000 (or $218,000 for a couple).
 See the  official CMS announcement  for complete IRMAA cutoff tables, as well as complete 2027 Medicare Part A and Part B programs premiums, deductibles, and coinsurance. The new amounts take effect on Jan. 1, 2027.
